layers.title: Wheel of Time (132 Years & Difficulty Ruler)
layers.artist_intent_A: 132-year issuance span (2009-2140) in 4-year halving cycles with geometrically stepping capsule heights (year 1 shortest -> year 4 tallest) and inner ruler ticks (each small box = 10 difficulty adjustments).
layers.verified_V: 132 contiguous years 2009..2140 clockwise from 12:00. Ideal 10-min target gives 3.9954 yr/halving (33 nonzero eras = 131.8 yr).
layers.inference_I: 34 sections x 4 years = 136 vs 132 displayed because era 34 (2141+) is a terminal zero-subsidy boundary.

layers.title: Geometric Halving Issuance Cutouts & Halving Crest
layers.artist_intent_A: Punched-out arc windows sized proportionally to BTC issued each halving era (50% in Era 1, halving thereafter), topped by Bitcoin Core's GetBlockSubsidy summation crest.
layers.verified_V: Crest formula sum_{i=0}^{32} 210000*floor(50e8/2^i)/10^8 = 20,999,999.97690000 BTC exact. Alpha-channel cutout measurement on master PNG yields 16 open-alpha slots (major 7 widths: 119.5°, 63.5°, 30.9°, 15.3°, 7.7°, 4.1°, 2.2° -> ratios 1.88-2.06 around ~120°/2^k) + 18 dark laser slits = 34 eras. Walnut cutout dividers on v4.0 physically carry engraved halving-year labels (2009, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024, 2028, 2032, 2036 - 2140).
layers.inference_I: Era 0 is scaled to ~120° (1/3 circle) rather than 180° so the 12:00 Halving Crest (~28°) and 27 narrow terminal slits fit cleanly around 360°.

alpha_cutout_measurements.note: Measured directly from RGBA alpha == 0 openings in FractalEncrypt_FullNode_v4_original.png. Because the 34 halving eras share 360 deg with the ~28-deg Halving Crest and 27 terminal kerf slits, Era 0 (2009) is scaled to ~120 deg (1/3 circle: measured 119.50 deg) and halves closely along 120 -> 60 -> 30 -> 15 -> 7.5 -> 3.75 -> 1.88 deg (measured 119.50, 63.50, 30.90, 15.30, 7.70, 4.10, 2.20 deg; ratios 1.88, 2.06, 2.02, 1.99, 1.88, 1.86) separated by ~2.4-deg wooden spokes. Followed by 9 narrower open-alpha slits (1.30..0.30 deg) + 18 dark laser slits (16 + 18 = 34 total eras).

layers.title: Binary Encoded ASCII Ring
layers.artist_intent_A: Hidden binary Easter-egg messages separated into 3 arcs by the 3 Pillar Crests.
layers.verified_V: Plain 8-bit ASCII (60 bytes / 480 bits, zero cipher): Arc A 'stock to flow ratio' (19 B), Arc B 'Craig Wright is a Fraud' (23 B), Arc C 'Bitcoin Fixes This' (18 B). Blind unsupervised 2D NCC agrees 471/480 (98.12%); 9/9 diffs optically verified against pixels.
layers.inference_I: Replaces v1 schematic's original Arc A/C ('Everything Divided by 21 Million' / 'We Are All Satoshi'). Third-party Gemini PDF's 91-byte decode is a confirmed hallucination.

layers.title: Merkle Trees, Three Pillars, 18 Polyhedra & 'BTC' Badges
layers.artist_intent_A: 21 Merkle/mycelium trees (3x7) linked by 18 geometric 'blocks' + 3 Pillar Crests (Social, Technical, Financial) = 21 elements representing Bitcoin's foundations.
layers.verified_V: All 18 polyhedra optically identified as the COMPLETE set of 5 Platonic + 13 Archimedean solids (5+13=18). Three Pillar Crests carry COMMUNITY / Y^2 = X^3 + 7 / GOLD 2.0 and lower 8-bit ASCII badges 01000010 ('B'), 01010100 ('T'), 01000011 ('C') = 'BTC'. Each of the 21 tree crowns embeds a miniature B symbol.
layers.inference_I: Financial sector merges Tweet 18/n's 'Portability' and 'Divisibility' into 'PORTABLE & DIVISIBLE' to preserve exact 6-label symmetry per sector.

layers.inference_I: 52,500 blocks/yr (210,000/4) was chosen over 52,560 (365*144) so halvings land cleanly on 4-year multiples.

layers.title: Satoshi's Whitepaper Equations (Section 11)
layers.artist_intent_A: Contains all mathematical equations from Section 11 (Calculations) of Satoshi Nakamoto's 2008 Bitcoin white paper.
layers.verified_V: Exact 180-degree twofold rotational symmetry tiling 5 equation blocks twice = 10 blocks around 360° (Eq4, Eq3, Eq4, Eq1, Eq2 x2). On v4, Eti_4IHWgAAnPy4.jpg, AND the 2022 84"x40" Blueprint Canvas, lambda, e^{-lambda}, '1' (rendered as ','), and 'k=0' ('k=>') drop out identically.
layers.inference_I: PDF TeX/Symbol font glyphs dropped during original Illustrator CAD vector import and remained baked into the master file.

interactive_data.symmetry: Exact 180-degree twofold rotational symmetry (5 equation blocks repeated twice = 10 total blocks around 360 deg).
clockwise_sequence_per_180_deg: Eq4 (rearranged catch-up sum: 1 - sum_{k=0}^z (lambda^k e^{-lambda} / k!)(1 - (q/p)^{z-k}))
Eq3 (infinite tail sum: sum_{k=0}^inf (lambda^k e^{-lambda} / k!){(q/p)^{z-k} if k<=z; 1 if k>z})
Eq1 (gambler's ruin: q_z = {1 if p<=q; (q/p)^z if p>q})
interactive_data.dropout_note: Confirmed on scarce_city_blueprint_canvas_1 (4608x3456) that lambda, e^{-lambda}, 1 (rendered as ','), and 'k=0' (rendered as 'k=>') remain dropped even on the 2022 84x40-inch Blueprint Canvas, proving the Symbol glyph dropout persists in the Illustrator master.

Q22.title: Layer 14 Concentric Planispheric Astrolabe Solar Calendar (Kepler's 2nd Law, e=0.0174)
Q22.summary: Pure-K sub-pixel geometry on 351 single-day intervals proves Layer 14's uneven day-tick spacing implements Kepler's 2nd Law of planetary motion: 1st-harmonic fit recovers Earth's orbital eccentricity e = 0.0174 (true 0.01671), Perihelion = Jan 3-4 (1.023 deg/day; Dec 31.78 deg), Aphelion = Jul 5 (0.954 deg/day; Jul 29.60 deg — 2.18 deg narrower than Dec despite both having 31 days), with Solstices & Equinoxes on exact cardinal axes (3:00 Vernal, 12:00 Summer, 9:00 Autumnal, 6:00 Winter). All 12 full-span month dividers point radially to the wheel center (intersect within 2.6 px, not eccentric).

Q25.title: 8abc4134 Wood-Grain Core Mismatch (Different Physical Build / Pre-Replacement Core)
Q25.summary: Upright-aligned wood-grain comparison proves Scarce City listing photo 8abc4134 (v4_2) is NOT the final v4.0 core seen in 3c6cea38, v4_original, and a44: 8abc4134 exhibits 90-degree-rotated horizontal walnut grain beneath C01 captions (vs identical vertical walnut grain on 3c6cea38/v4_original/a44), 6 completely unengraved blank maple reward cells (50..1.562), and a ~30 deg different Layer 13 glue-up angle.

DF75_DF76.title: Physical v4.0 vs Draft Eti_4ItXAAQTSjx (t07) & Final EtjAQyOXIAIoIbk (t08)
DF75_DF76.summary: Physical v4.0 (v4_original) carries BOTH the 34 hollow outer-edge diamonds on Ring 7 (DF75) AND heavy beveled/chamfered year-cell outlines on Ring 2 (DF76), matching final t08 (EtjAQyOXIAIoIbk). elements.meaning: 8-bit ASCII for 'stock to flow ratio', the quantity behind the formulas of ring 8. It is row 15 of the artist's table of candidate 'Easter eggs', a row he did not mark as used.
elements.notes: phi range is the crop of the strip, slightly wider than the text. Read by eye from the rectified strip. Checked by a second, machine reading (scripts/blind_bit_reader.py, results/blind_bit_reader.json): it sorts the glyph cells of the strip into two classes without the reading by eye and is compared with it afterwards. 146 of the 152 cells of this arc agree; in the other 6 it differs, and its text reads "stock'wo!flow ratio" where the reading by eye has "stock to flow ratio". The reading by eye stands there: it gives plain words in every byte (I); the cells are shown in evidence/blind_bit_reader_disagreements.png. Until 2026-11-22 this note said 'not yet machine-checked' (corrected in package KB). Geometry converted in P1 from the ellipse frame of wheel_binary_ring.py to the design frame (scripts/l04_to_design_frame.py). The evidence strip is still the ellipse-frame crop. | P3: The 19 bytes of arc A, read as 0 and 1 on the rectified strip of the main photo (evidence/binary_ring_arc_A.png) and decoded as 8-bit ASCII. The bits are typed in scripts/wheel_binary_ring.py, which writes results/binary_ring_decoded.json; scripts/transcribe.py takes bits and hex from there and stops if they do not decode to this text. The reading was made with that script and stood only in the record until package DT2 (2026-11-22), when it got this row. Read again that day, byte by byte, on the sheet (the strip in 5 rows, zoom 3): every byte as typed. The machine reader scripts/blind_bit_reader.py, which does not know the typed bits, gives 146 of its 152 bits; the six others, in bytes 5, 6 and 8 counted from 0, read 0 on the sheet, as typed (results/blind_bit_reader.json). The record's older note 'not yet machine-checked' was written before that reader existed. Bits compared by eye with the artist's table: identical. The artist's text says the highlighted rows were used; this row is NOT highlighted. Photo and line art both carry it, so on this point the legend does not describe the v4 piece.

elements.label: outer ruler row: 343 fine marks
elements.meaning: The fine marks of the 'Halving Ruler': 343, evenly spaced (counted on the line art and, one by one, on the piece), one fewer than the 344 small marks of ring 2. The artist: the ruler tracks every 2,016 blocks. 343 marks is about one mark per ten adjustments (3,437 adjustments in all).
elements.notes: 343 marks (package AHR, 2026-11-21): counted one by one on the line art t06, which has no number badge, median spacing 1.050 degrees = 360 / 343, no gap (the vector project measured the same). Unrolled about the row's own drawing centre, about 3 key px right of the key centre, its spectrum peaks at 343; on evidence/layers/L12/strip_design.png, which is unrolled about the key centre, a plain spectrum splits into 342 and 344 and the direct count of row 36 is 343 all the same (package AHS, 2026-11-21, after the review of AHR). Earlier: counted by scripts/count_marks.py on the colour key, 337 found plus 7 taken as hidden by the number badge = 344 (results/ruler_counts.json); the badge hides 6. The ring is about 6 key px off-centre in the schematic, so the counter follows the row.

elements.label: formula block 1 of 10: sum with two cases in braces

engraved.text: SUM(k=>..inf) [ k over k! ] . { (q/p)^(z-k)  if k<=z ;  ,  if k>z }

expected.value: sum over k = 0..infinity of  lambda^k e^-lambda / k!  times  { (q/p)^(z-k) if k <= z ; 1 if k > z }
expected.detail: Bitcoin whitepaper, section 11 (Calculations), https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf

elements.meaning: From section 11 of the whitepaper: the probability that an attacker still catches up after z blocks, as a Poisson-weighted sum over the progress k he may have made. On the wheel the formula lacks lambda, e and the digit 1.
elements.notes: Extent read off the line art by eye. On the photographed piece this plate is turned 8.25 deg; the layer frame carries the turn. | P3: Read on the artist's colour key, unrolled at high zoom. Under the sum sign the design has k, an equals sign and an arrow-like glyph where the paper has 0; it is written k=> here. The earlier reading 'k=0' was taken at lower zoom and was wrong. The piece has the same glyph (formulas 3 to 9 are read on the piece). P8 K06 (2026-11-20): read by the main session on the artist's thread photo t02 (box 2358 848 2986 1519): the infinity sign above and k=> below the sum, k over k!, (q/p)^(z-k), a comma where 1 belongs, 'if k<=z' and 'if k>z' with the signs drawn as such; glyph for glyph the design reading. t02 is taken as the v4 piece by inference (map/picture_notes.json). Before K06: the same text read on t07_tw05_Eti_4ItXAAQTSjx.jpg (design, high). MISMATCH: The structure is the whitepaper formula, but glyphs are missing on the wheel: no lambda, no e, and a comma or nothing where the whitepaper has the digit 1. The reading stands (line art and photo agree); it looks like a font that lacked those glyphs.

v4_overrides.title: Layer 14 Concentric Planispheric Astrolabe Solar Calendar (Kepler's 2nd Law, e=0.0174)
v4_overrides.summary: Pure-K sub-pixel geometry on 351 single-day intervals proves Layer 14's uneven day-tick spacing implements Kepler's 2nd Law of planetary motion: 1st-harmonic fit recovers Earth's orbital eccentricity e = 0.0174 (true 0.01671), Perihelion = Jan 3-4 (1.023 deg/day; Dec 31.78 deg), Aphelion = Jul 5 (0.954 deg/day; Jul 29.60 deg — 2.18 deg narrower than Dec despite both having 31 days), with Solstices & Equinoxes on exact cardinal axes (3:00 Vernal, 12:00 Summer, 9:00 Autumnal, 6:00 Winter). All 12 full-span month dividers point radially to the wheel center (intersect within 2.6 px, not eccentric).

elements.label: bottom strip of the square frame, with divisions
elements.meaning: Divided strip along the bottom of the square plate. On the artist's colour key and on his figure for layers 16 to 19 its left half has the colour of field 18 and its right half the colour of field 19, not the grey of field 16. Its divisions were counted on the piece and on the colour key (2026-11-22): 7 cells in the left half, under Double Digit, and 12 cells in the right half, under Single Digit, 19 in all, with no text in them. What the 7 and the 12 count is not known: no source says, and nothing is claimed.
elements.notes: Part of the square plate, which is not a ring sector: the region is an approximation and covers the middle of the strip. On the colour key t07 and on the artist's figure t43 the strip is not the grey of field 16: its left half has the teal of field 18 and its right half the pink of field 19, as has the narrow band above it. By its colour the strip belongs to fields 18 and 19, half each; the record keeps its id in layer 16, because ids are permanent, and its region lies in the bands of layers 19 and 18 (package DT2, 2026-11-22). Its divisions, counted on the piece (the Scarce City photo 3c6cea38fbff4121ae6ef2eb0a058347eb474b52-4608x3456.jpg, the strip unrolled: evidence/reading_sheets/LE_3c6c_plate_bottom_strip.png) and on the colour key t07 (evidence/reading_sheets/LE_t07_plate_bottom_strip.png): 6 dividing lines and 7 cells in the left half, 11 dividing lines and 12 cells in the right half, 19 cells in all; the halves meet at the line that runs on up the plate between Double Digit and Single Digit, and the first and the last cell are cut by the mitre lines of the frame's corners. The piece and the key agree. No text stands in the cells (package LE, 2026-11-22).

elements.label: arc ruler, lower left, numbered 1 to 21
elements.meaning: The 'Bitcoin Issuance Ruler' (artist): 0 to 21, for 21 million bitcoin, on 22 stems from the bottom centre up the left side. Measured on the piece: the stems are the equal divisions of a straight scale seen from the centre of the wheel, angle = atan(n / 7). So 7 stands at 45 degrees, under the lower left corner of the square plate, and 21 = 3 x 7 at 71.6 degrees: the ruler is the lower edge of the square, carried on to three times its half length.
elements.notes: Numbers read on the artist's figure for layers 20-21 (evidence/reading_sheets/Q13_Q14_t44_rulers_and_captions.png): 1 at the bottom centre, 21 at the upper end, crowding towards the upper end. Marks not counted (question Q13). | P3: The text lists the numerals of the ruler that are readings of the piece by the standard of findings/DECISIONS.md (package AHS, 2026-11-21): a numeral is a reading of the piece only where every glyph of it shows its own shape on a piece photo; a filled round mark is not a reading. All four are read on the piece photo t02: 2 on evidence/reading_sheets/AHS_t02_L20_n01_n09.png (zoom 2.4; looked at again at 6 times), 10, 11 and 21 on evidence/reading_sheets/AHT_t02_L20_n09_n21.png (zoom 8, turned 119 degrees). Each numeral has a record of its own, L20.numeral.n01 to L20.numeral.n21, which holds its reading and its photo: L20.numeral.n02 and L20.numeral.n10 are read on t02, L20.numeral.n11 and L20.numeral.n21 on the rectified Scarce City photo source/extra/scarcecity/3c6cea38fbff4121ae6ef2eb0a058347eb474b52-4608x3456.jpg (evidence/reading_sheets/R7_sc3c6_rect_ruler_L20_end.png), and these two show their shapes on t02 as well. The 2 also reads on the Scarce City photo source/extra/scarcecity/8abc4134a6a46abf86643c1411b2ed0b64aa5e84-4608x3456.jpg (evidence/reading_sheets/AHT_sc8abc_L20_n01_n04.png, zoom 6). The other numerals of the ruler are not in this text: 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 12, 14, 16 and 18 are readings of the design render t41 in their own records (on the piece: a plain stroke at stem 1, marks at stems 3 to 9 that do not show their digits, filled but for a thinner hooked mark at stem 7, and at 12, 14, 16 and 18 a 1 and a second glyph that is a closed or a filled shape), and 5 is illegible (L20.numeral.n05). The ruler has 22 stems, numbers 0 to 21, clockwise from a zero stem at 179.7 degrees to 251.5 degrees; the stems 13, 15, 17, 19 and 20 carry no numeral, and none stands at the zero stem. Stem 7 stands under the lower left corner of the square plate (45 degrees from zero). Measured angles: evidence/reading_sheets/R7_sc3c6_rect_rulers_stems.json. Changed in package AHT (2026-11-22, approved by Idle after the review of package AHS). The reading of Run 7 (2026-11-19) that this replaces, moved here unchanged: text '10 11 12 14 16 18 21', read from source/extra/scarcecity/3c6cea38fbff4121ae6ef2eb0a058347eb474b52-4608x3456.jpg (piece, eye, medium), sheet evidence/reading_sheets/R7_sc3c6_rect_ruler_L20_end.png, with the note: 'Read on rectified strips of a Scarce City photo of the v4 piece (plane of the wooden disc fitted to 7 control points, RMS 2.2 px). The text lists the numerals that are legible. The ruler has 22 stems, numbers 0 to 21, clockwise from a zero stem at 179.7 degrees to 251.5 degrees. Stems 1 to 9 carry a round mark with a numeral that is not legible; 13, 15, 17, 19 and 20 carry none. Stem 7 stands under the lower left corner of the square plate (45 degrees from zero). Middle part: evidence/reading_sheets/R7_sc3c6_rect_ruler_L20_mid.png. Measured angles: evidence/reading_sheets/R7_sc3c6_rect_rulers_stems.json.' Of that list 12, 14, 16 and 18 do not meet the standard: on three photos of the piece their second glyph does not show its own shape.

elements.meaning: A numeral of the 'Bitcoin Issuance Ruler' (artist): it counts millions of bitcoin issued, 0 at the bottom centre to 21 million at the upper end. The stems follow angle = atan(n / 7) (measured on the piece); 1 to 12 are numbered, then 14, 16, 18 and 21.
elements.notes: Added in package AHR (2026-11-21) from the artist's render of the key's centre (t40 = t41, t44), where the numerals stand just outside the stems (evidence/reading_sheets/AHR_t41_L20_polar.png). Angle from the stem rule measured on the piece and on t41: stem 1 at 180 + atan(1 / 7) = 188.13 degrees up the left side, clockwise from the zero stem at 6 o'clock; radius about 290 to 300 key px, approximate. The full colour keys t01, t07, t08 and the line art t06 draw the stems without numerals. Region corrected in package LF (2026-11-23), by measurement on the artist's centre render t41 (base key_centre; its ruler lines stand where they stand on the keys t07 and t08 and on the line art, within 0.25 key px, so its registration is right here): on t41 the glyph lies at r 285.0 to 292.0 key px and phi 187.37 to 187.89 degrees, beside the stem at 188.13, outside the ruler's outer line at r 283.75; the region is the glyph widened by 0.15 degrees on each side, from 0.75 key px outside the line to 1 key px beyond the glyph. The region was phi 187.43 to 188.83, r 290 to 300 key px, which held 24 percent of the glyph's ink. On the photo of number 4 the mark of the numeral lies in the new region (scripts/core_regions_check.py, results/core_regions_key_centre.json; sheets evidence/reading_sheets/LF_before_key_centre_L20_numerals.png and LF_before_photo_L20_numerals.png). Added by hand on 2026-11-21 (map/additions.json). | P3: A reading of the design render t41 (also t44). On the piece the stems 1 to 9 carry small marks: a plain stroke at stem 1, a mark that reads as a 2 at stem 2 (L20.numeral.n02), and filled round marks at stems 3 to 9 whose digits are not legible (t02: evidence/reading_sheets/AHS_t02_L20_n01_n09.png, zoom 2.4, and AHR_t02_L20_numerals_1_9.png; the Scarce City photo: evidence/reading_sheets/R7_sc3c6_rect_ruler_L20_mid.png). AHR, 2026-11-21; the sentence on the piece reworded in package AHS (2026-11-21): the note of AHR said the digits of all the marks 1 to 9 are not legible. One standard for both rulers (findings/DECISIONS.md, package AHS, 2026-11-21): a numeral is a reading of the piece only where every glyph of it shows its own shape on a piece photo; a filled round mark is not a reading. Compared: equal, ignoring case, spacing and punctuation.

elements.meaning: A numeral of the 'Bitcoin Issuance Ruler' (artist): it counts millions of bitcoin issued, 0 at the bottom centre to 21 million at the upper end. The stems follow angle = atan(n / 7) (measured on the piece); 1 to 12 are numbered, then 14, 16, 18 and 21.
elements.notes: Added in package AHR (2026-11-21) from the artist's render of the key's centre (t40 = t41, t44), where the numerals stand just outside the stems (evidence/reading_sheets/AHR_t41_L20_polar.png). Angle from the stem rule measured on the piece and on t41: stem 4 at 180 + atan(4 / 7) = 209.74 degrees up the left side, clockwise from the zero stem at 6 o'clock; radius about 290 to 300 key px, approximate. The full colour keys t01, t07, t08 and the line art t06 draw the stems without numerals. Region corrected in package LF (2026-11-23), by measurement on the artist's centre render t41 (base key_centre; its ruler lines stand where they stand on the keys t07 and t08 and on the line art, within 0.25 key px, so its registration is right here): on t41 the glyph lies at r 284.0 to 291.25 key px and phi 208.86 to 209.6 degrees, beside the stem at 209.74, outside the ruler's outer line at r 282.75; the region is the glyph widened by 0.15 degrees on each side, from 0.75 key px outside the line to 1 key px beyond the glyph. The region was phi 209.04 to 210.44, r 290 to 300 key px, which held 9 percent of the glyph's ink. On the photo of number 4 the mark of the numeral lies in the new region (scripts/core_regions_check.py, results/core_regions_key_centre.json; sheets evidence/reading_sheets/LF_before_key_centre_L20_numerals.png and LF_before_photo_L20_numerals.png). Added by hand on 2026-11-21 (map/additions.json). | P3: A reading of the design render t41 (also t44). On the piece the stems 1 to 9 carry small marks: a plain stroke at stem 1, a mark that reads as a 2 at stem 2 (L20.numeral.n02), and filled round marks at stems 3 to 9 whose digits are not legible (t02: evidence/reading_sheets/AHS_t02_L20_n01_n09.png, zoom 2.4, and AHR_t02_L20_numerals_1_9.png; the Scarce City photo: evidence/reading_sheets/R7_sc3c6_rect_ruler_L20_mid.png). One standard for both rulers (findings/DECISIONS.md, package AHS, 2026-11-21): a numeral is a reading of the piece only where every glyph of it shows its own shape on a piece photo; a filled round mark is not a reading. Compared: equal, ignoring case, spacing and punctuation.

elements.label: overlay digit on L07.e29

expected.detail: digital root of the exact subsidy 50 / 2^29 BTC: halving multiplies a digital root by 5, which gives the cycle 5, 7, 8, 4, 2, 1

elements.meaning: Third-party overlay digit on a reward cell, not on the sculpture: the digital root of the exact subsidy 50 / 2^n. Halving multiplies a digital root by 5, so the ring shows the cycle 5, 7, 8, 4, 2, 1. From era 10 on the engraved subsidy is cut to whole satoshi and has another digital root; the overlay ignores that.
elements.notes: The inventory found 31 of the 34 overlay digits of ring 7 on the small image; this one is too small there. It is on the 1400 x 1414 image (evidence/reading_sheets/R7d_level39_ring7_d.png). Placed like its neighbours, one cell further. Added by hand on 2026-11-19 (map/additions.json). | P3: Read on the 1400 x 1414 copy of the overlay image, ring 7 unrolled. On this ring the digits are not 3, 6, 9; each of the six values has its own colour (5 red, 7 orange, 8 olive, 4 green, 2 blue-green, 1 blue). The digit is small here; shape and colour agree. Compared with the cycle of the exact halving: equal. The number engraved under it is the subsidy cut to whole satoshi (9 satoshi), whose digital root is 9: the overlay digit does not belong to the engraved number but to the uncut halving.

rules.meaning: Title of the piece, on the outer row of layer 1. The artist calls this row the constant part: it does not change from block to block.
One of four community mottos on the constant outer row (the artist: Bitcoin 'ethos' at the top of ring 1). Not data.
Caption of the status field on the tab below it. The inner row is the artist's 'current network state': the values of the chain tip, frozen at block 630,000.
Caption of the block hash that follows it on the same tab.
Hash of block 630,000, the block the piece is frozen at: all 64 characters equal the chain, 19 leading zeros.
Height of the block the piece is frozen at. Block 630,000 is the first block of the fourth reward era (third halving), the first with a subsidy of 6.25 BTC.
Header time of block 630,000 in UTC, to the minute (the full time is 19:23:43).
Difficulty of block 630,000, integer part (16,104,807,485,529.38).
Nonce in the header of block 630,000.
Number of transactions in block 630,000, the coinbase included.
Serialised size of block 630,000: 1,186,930 bytes, shown in kilobytes of 1,000 bytes. It is the size of the whole block, not of its transactions alone.
Weight of block 630,000: 3,993,250 weight units of the 4,000,000 allowed, shown in thousands.
What the miner of block 630,000 received: 6.25 BTC subsidy plus 0.90968084 BTC fees = 7.15968084, rounded to two decimals.

Bitcoin issued when block 630,000 arrived: the subsidies of blocks 0 to 629,999 by the schedule (10.5 + 5.25 + 2.625 million). It ignores the unspendable genesis output and coinbases that claimed less than allowed.
Version of the node software the artist put on the piece. Bitcoin Core 0.19.1 was the current release on 11 May 2020; his article text says 0.19.0.
A network-state value the artist recorded for the moment of block 630,000. It is not block data and has no single source, so it cannot be checked against the chain.
Calendar year {year} on the 'Wheel of Time': one of 132 cells from 2009 to 2140, the span in which the subsidy runs out. The cells step up in height through each four-year halving cycle.
The larger ruler marks under the year cells: one division per calendar year (artist). 132 divisions counted.
The smaller ruler marks: each stands for ten difficulty adjustments (artist). 344 marks counted, 86 per quadrant, evenly spaced; 6,930,000 blocks / 20,160 = 343.75.
The 'Halving Crest' at the top of the issuance ring; it carries the formula of the subsidy schedule.

The total the subsidy schedule can ever pay: 210,000 blocks per era times the subsidy cut to whole satoshi, summed over eras 0 to 32 and divided by 10^8 = 20,999,999.9769 BTC. The artist takes it from the Bitcoin Wiki page on controlled supply.
Cut-out window for reward era {n}: its size stands for the bitcoin issued in that era (artist). Measured {width} degrees wide; each window is half as wide as the one before.
Cut-out for reward era {n}, drawn as a slit: by the halving rule its width would be too small to show. The 24 slits stand 2.7 degrees apart.
Label for all remaining eras together: era 8 starts in 2036 by the wheel's four-year rule, and the subsidy ends in 2140.
Start year of the reward era whose cut-out begins here, by the wheel's rule of four years per era.
8-bit ASCII for 'stock to flow ratio', the quantity behind the formulas of ring 8. It is row 15 of the artist's table of candidate 'Easter eggs', a row he did not mark as used.
8-bit ASCII for 'Craig Wright is a Fraud'. The artist says one of the binary strings refers to 'Faketoshi'; it is row 17 of his table, marked as used.
8-bit ASCII for the community slogan 'Bitcoin Fixes This'. It is row 14 of the artist's table of candidates, a row he did not mark as used.
A word set over the Social crest: COMMUNITY. The artist's legend names the pillar, not this word; we read it as the heading of the pillar.
The equation of the curve secp256k1 that Bitcoin's keys and signatures use: y squared = x cubed + 7. It stands over the Technical crest.
A phrase set over the Financial crest: GOLD 2.0, bitcoin as a second, digital gold. Our reading of the phrase; the legend does not explain it.
Eight binary digits, one 8-bit ASCII code like the bytes of the binary ring: 01000010 is the letter B. The three crest bytes, clockwise from the top, spell BTC.
Eight binary digits, one 8-bit ASCII code like the bytes of the binary ring: 01010100 is the letter T. The three crest bytes, clockwise from the top, spell BTC.
Eight binary digits, one 8-bit ASCII code like the bytes of the binary ring: 01000011 is the letter C. The three crest bytes, clockwise from the top, spell BTC.
A label of the crest drawing, the word LOADING with four dots, mirrored left and right of the logo. We take it as decoration in the style of a loading screen; the artist does not comment on it.
Crest of the {pillar} pillar, one of the artist's 'Three Pillars of Bitcoin'. The three crests and the 18 solids make 21.
Name of the pillar: {pillar}. The six property labels that follow clockwise belong to it.
One of 21 Merkle trees, in three groups of seven. For version 4 the artist redrew the tree so that it also reads as a mushroom with mycelium.

One of 18 'blocks' that link the trees, drawn as a solid (artist). Probably the {gloss}: the drawing shows its kinds of faces, and it is one of the three Archimedean solids left when the other fifteen are identified.

One of 18 'blocks' that link the trees, drawn as a solid because every block is unique (artist). This one is the {gloss}, identified from its faces on the colour key. The 18 are the five Platonic and the thirteen Archimedean solids, each once.
A property of the {pillar} pillar. The artist's gloss: {gloss}.
Block height the wheel gives for the end of {year}: 52,500 blocks per year from 2009, a quarter of a 210,000-block era. It is a schedule, not the chain.{real}

A short laddered bridge (two rails with rungs) that joins two neighbouring reward plates; it carries no text. It stands only at 6 o'clock, between the plates of reward eras 17 and 18 (the eras the wheel starts in 2072 and 2076; the halving between them is block 3,570,000), and lines up with the bridge of ring 10.

A short laddered bridge (two rails with rungs) that joins two neighbouring supply plates; it carries no text. It stands only at 6 o'clock, between the plates of eras 17 and 18, and lines up with the bridge of ring 7.

A row of 34 small hollow diamonds on the ring's outer line, one over each joint of two reward plates (counted on the line art). It carries no text. The artist's render of this place draws the line and its diamonds in blue, apart from the black lines of the engraving; on the piece photo t31 a diamond shows at each of the two plate joints in the frame.

A single small chevron on the ring's inner line at 12 o'clock, under the joint of the last and the first supply plate (eras 34 and 1). Measured on the line art: no other joint has one. By its place it marks the seam where the ring begins (an interpretation). It carries no text.

The long marks of the year ruler: at every fourth year division a line crosses the blank band to the difficulty ruler. 33 of them, before 2009, 2013, 2017 and so on to 2137, so they group the 132 years in fours from 2009 (counted on the line art). Every second division has a slightly longer tick (66). The outer ends of the long lines alternate between two lengths.
The 34th cell: no subsidy. From block 6,930,000 on the protocol pays nothing; the artist counts this zero era as the 34th.
Block subsidy of reward era {n} (blocks {first} to {last}): 50 BTC halved {era_no} times and cut to whole satoshi, as the protocol does.
A phrase the artist credits to Matt Odell on TFTC (he also points to Nic Carter's 'A Most Peaceful Revolution'). The ring has THE where his text has A.
Title of Knut Svanholm's book 'Bitcoin: Sovereignty Through Mathematics', without its first word.
The newspaper headline Satoshi put into the coinbase of block 0, between two '//' marks. Letter for letter the text on the chain.
PlanB's stock-to-flow regression of March 2019 for the market value. The artist added the stock-to-flow formulas after a tweet by Saifedean Ammous of 27 December 2020.
The per-coin form of the stock-to-flow model, which the artist takes from a live S2F chart.
The model-price formula a second time, turned round to end in 'X USD'. The legend lists two formulas; this third string is not mentioned there.
Title of a row of this ring: bitcoin issued per day, or per year, in each reward era.
Issue per day in the zero era: nothing.
Issue per year in the zero era: nothing.
Bitcoin issued per day in reward era {n}: the subsidy of {subsidy} BTC times 144 blocks. An ideal ten-minute day, not a measured one.
Bitcoin issued per year in reward era {n}: the subsidy of {subsidy} BTC times 144 blocks times 365 days (52,560 blocks). Ring 6 counts 52,500 blocks a year; the two rings use different years.
The year the wheel gives reward era {n} as its start: 2009 for the first, then four years apart from 2012.
The nominal cap, 21 million. The artist: by the 34th era all 21 million are mined. By the protocol the total is 20,999,999.9769 BTC.
Bitcoin issued by the end of reward era {n}: 21,000,000 x (1 - 2^-{n}). The ring shows the schedule without the satoshi floor, to one or two decimals.

An ornament at the top of the ring: a Bitcoin logo between the words SCANNING and MEMPOOL, each with a row of dots. The legend does not mention it. It sits where the arrow from the 50 BTC points, so it may stand for the transaction waiting in the mempool to be mined.
Caption in the artist's picture of the first transaction: a 50 BTC output is spent, 10 BTC go to the receiver and 40 BTC come back as change.
Hal Finney's key in address form: output 0 of the block-170 transaction, 10 BTC. The output pays to a public key; the address is how explorers show it.
Output 1 of the block-170 transaction, 40 BTC, to the same key that paid: the change goes back to the sender.
The key whose 50 BTC the transaction spends: the coinbase output of block 9, Satoshi's.
Amount of output 0: what Hal Finney received.
Amount of output 1: the change. 10 + 40 = 50, so the transaction paid no fee.
Amount of the output being spent: one whole block subsidy of 2009.
Arrow from the spent 50 BTC clockwise towards the two outputs: the direction of the payment.
The block that holds the first transaction between two people.
The date the artist gives for the first transaction. Block 170 has header time 2009-01-12 03:30:25 UTC, which is the evening of 11 January in the Americas.
Block height on the halving ruler: every second halving, 210,000 + 420,000 x {n0}. Two reward eras lie between one number and the next.

Small year label in the middle of the segment of reward era {n}. The label is 2010 + 4 x {n0}: the wheel year that ends at the middle of the era (an era is four wheel years from 2009). The 34th label, 2142, lies beyond the last year of ring 2.

The fine marks of the 'Halving Ruler': 343, evenly spaced (counted on the line art and, one by one, on the piece), one fewer than the 344 small marks of ring 2. The artist: the ruler tracks every 2,016 blocks. 343 marks is about one mark per ten adjustments (3,437 adjustments in all).
136 boxes, four per reward era: the 34 eras divided into years of the wheel.
34 long marks, one per 210,000 blocks: the halvings (artist: every 210,000 blocks between halvings).
From section 11 of the whitepaper: {gloss}. On the wheel the formula lacks lambda, e and the digit 1.
A day number on the calendar ring: every tenth day of a month carries its number, 10, 20 and 30 (February 10 and 20). The days run anticlockwise, like the months; the number stands at its day mark.
A month of the ordinary calendar ('month and day, for use in linked timestamping', artist). The months run anticlockwise; this segment is {width} degrees wide.

Day marks of the calendar ring: 365, and each month segment holds exactly the days of its month (February 28). The artist's text says 365.4 days. The marks are not evenly spaced: 0.953 degrees apart in June at the top, 1.026 in December at the bottom.
Middle row of the calendar ring: steps of ten days. On the piece they are numbered 10, 20, 30 within each month (records L14.day_numeral).
Caption on the inner edge of the calendar plate, above the half disc with the ten arcs: it names what the arcs are about, the ten-minute block time (the artist's layer 15, 'Block Confirmation Time').

The number of a minute, 1 to 10, at the rim end of one of the ten arcs: the artist calls them 'the numbered minutes' of the ten minute block time (launch stream, 59:46). The numbers run clockwise, 1 to 5 on the left of 12 o'clock and 6 to 10 on the right.
One of ten arcs in the upper half disc: the artist's picture of block times spread around ten minutes (he calls it the Poisson distribution of block confirmation times).
The Bitcoin logo at the centre of the 'main circle', where the artist put the genesis block. Mirror acrylic on the piece.
Hash of block 0. The artist's text calls it the 'Block 0 Transaction Hash'; on the chain it is the block hash.
Merkle root of block 0 in internal byte order, as it stands in chainparams.cpp. Reversed it is also the id of the one transaction of the block.
Address form of the public key that the coinbase of block 0 pays to ('Satoshi's first address'). Its 50 BTC cannot be spent.
The last 11 bytes of the genesis public key in reversed byte order. The artist labels it scriptPubKey; it is a fragment of the key, not a script.
Part of the plate the artist numbers 16: the inner half ring with its spokes, together with the square frame round the reward-era picture. The half ring carries no text.
Caption on the frame of plate 16: the number of reward eras as the artist counts them, 33 with a subsidy plus the zero era.
Caption on the frame of plate 16: the eras that pay less than one bitcoin per block. 27 eras with a subsidy (0.78125 BTC down to one satoshi) plus the zero era make the 28 bars of the fan.

Divided strip along the bottom of the square plate. On the artist's colour key and on his figure for layers 16 to 19 its left half has the colour of field 18 and its right half the colour of field 19, not the grey of field 16. Its divisions were counted on the piece and on the colour key (2026-11-22): 7 cells in the left half, under Double Digit, and 12 cells in the right half, under Single Digit, 19 in all, with no text in them. What the 7 and the 12 count is not known: no source says, and nothing is claimed.

Fan bar {n} of 28, counted from the right end. By its place it holds the subsidy of reward era {era_n} ({subsidy} BTC). The number is hidden by a number badge in the artist's figure; on the photos of the piece the bar is engraved, but not every digit of it is legible, so it is not recorded as read.

Fan bar {n} of 28, counted from the right end: the block subsidy of reward era {era_n} ({subsidy} BTC), cut to whole satoshi. The fan runs from 0.78125 BTC at the left end to zero at the right end: the artist's 28 eras below one bitcoin.
Subsidy of one of the three 'double-digit' reward eras: 50, 25 and 12.5 BTC.

Subsidy of one of the three 'single-digit' reward eras: 6.25, 3.125 and 1.5625 BTC. The third is cut to 1.562 on the piece and to 1.56 on the artist's design figure. The era of block 630,000 is the first of them.
The artist's name for the first three eras, whose subsidy has two digits before the point.
The artist's name for eras four to six, whose subsidy has one digit before the point.

A numeral of the 'Bitcoin Issuance Ruler' (artist): it counts millions of bitcoin issued, 0 at the bottom centre to 21 million at the upper end. The stems follow angle = atan(n / 7) (measured on the piece); 1 to 12 are numbered, then 14, 16, 18 and 21.

A numeral of the 'Bitcoin Halving Era Ruler' (artist): it counts reward eras from the bottom centre. The stems follow angle = atan(n / 12) (measured on the piece); 1 to 10 are numbered, then 12 to 20 in steps of two, then 24, 28 and 34. The ruler has 33 stems, 0 to 32, so the numeral 34 stands at stem 32.

The 'Bitcoin Issuance Ruler' (artist): 0 to 21, for 21 million bitcoin, on 22 stems from the bottom centre up the left side. Measured on the piece: the stems are the equal divisions of a straight scale seen from the centre of the wheel, angle = atan(n / 7). So 7 stands at 45 degrees, under the lower left corner of the square plate, and 21 = 3 x 7 at 71.6 degrees: the ruler is the lower edge of the square, carried on to three times its half length.

The 'Bitcoin Halving Era Ruler' (artist): the reward eras 0 to 34 from the bottom centre up the right side (halvings 35 to 64 pay nothing and are left out). Measured on the piece: the stems are the equal divisions of a straight scale seen from the centre of the wheel, angle = atan(n / 12). So 12 stands at 45 degrees, under the lower right corner of the square plate. The ruler has 33 stems, 0 to 32 (the last at 69.4 degrees from the zero stem; the piece's ruler ends at 69.2), and its last numeral, 34, stands at stem 32 (AHR, 2026-11-21: counted on the render t41 and on the line art). Numbered: 1 to 10, 12 to 20 in steps of two, 24, 28, 34.
A total engraved under the square plate: the 132 calendar years of the wheel, 2009 to 2140.
A total: 34 reward eras, the artist's count (33 with a subsidy plus the zero era).

The rule behind the ruler rings: the difficulty is adjusted every 2,016 blocks. The piece gives no count on this line. The artist's design figure has 'Difficulty Adjustments: 3437 (Every 2016 Blocks)': 6,930,000 / 2,016 = 3,437.5, so 3,437 counts the adjustments up to the last block with a subsidy.
A total: the nominal cap of 21 million. By the protocol the sum of all subsidies is 20,999,999.9769 BTC.

Third-party overlay digit on a reward cell, not on the sculpture: the digital root of the exact subsidy 50 / 2^n. Halving multiplies a digital root by 5, so the ring shows the cycle 5, 7, 8, 4, 2, 1. From era 10 on the engraved subsidy is cut to whole satoshi and has another digital root; the overlay ignores that.
Third-party overlay digit, not on the sculpture: the digital root of the number under it (expected {exp}). It adds no information of its own.

glossary.L05.property.social_1: the anonymous founder who published the whitepaper, kept perfect operational security and left
glossary.L05.property.social_2: an origin without a leader or inventor to pressure, which cannot be repeated
glossary.L05.property.social_3: Bitcoin is free and open-source software
glossary.L05.property.social_4: no central control; he points to Stratum V2 for mining pools
glossary.L05.property.social_5: no third parties or mediators between the two sides of a payment
glossary.L05.property.social_6: his view that Bitcoin pays for cheap, clean energy; he says himself that this is a contested inclusion
glossary.L05.property.technical_1: Hashcash-style proof of work, credited to Adam Back
glossary.L05.property.technical_2: three of the eight references of the whitepaper are about linked timestamping
glossary.L05.property.technical_3: the hash trees that let a node check the chain back to the first block
glossary.L05.property.technical_4: the signature scheme behind keys, addresses and signed transactions
glossary.L05.property.technical_6: the retarget every 2,016 blocks that keeps blocks ten minutes apart whatever the hash power
glossary.L05.property.financial_1: the hard cap of 21 million made possible by scarcity in a digital thing
glossary.L05.property.financial_2: it does not rust, age or degrade
glossary.L05.property.financial_3: one unit is as good as another
glossary.L05.property.financial_4: a full node checks authenticity at once, without an assay or a third party
glossary.L05.property.financial_5: it can be moved and split into change
glossary.L05.property.financial_6: Nick Szabo's 'unforgeable costliness': nobody gets bitcoin without work, and the cost cannot be faked
glossary.L13.sum: the probability that an attacker still catches up after z blocks, as a Poisson-weighted sum over the progress k he may have made
glossary.L13.tail: the same probability rearranged so that the sum is finite (one minus a sum up to z)
glossary.L13.qz: the probability that an attacker ever catches up from z blocks behind
glossary.L13.lam: the expected progress of the attacker while the honest chain adds z blocks

artist_gui_portal_checklist.detail: Floating glassmorphic Left & Right Zoomed Telemetry Containers flanking the wheel (toggleable HUD) display active block & era metrics while inspecting.

hallucination_guardrails: Do NOT use third-party Gemini PDF Layer 4 binary decode ('sovereigntythroughmathematics' / 91 B — fabricated; physical v4 is 60 B: 'stock to flow ratio' | 'Craig Wright is a Fraud' | 'Bitcoin Fixes This').

Do NOT use secondary prose typos for v4.0 Block 630,000 ('276.56 GB', '$8,651.77', '119 vMB', '11.9 MB', '686,985'); physical v4 pixels read '276.95 GB', '$8,657.77', '1.19 VMB' (crisp decimal dot optically confirmed across v4_4, EtjAgf4XAAAp_fd & Exq2unjWgAIow9X, Q02), '686,885'. NOTE: Edition #1 (Block 600,000, BM a45) DOES genuinely read 'MEMPOOL SIZE 11.9 MB' and 'UNMINED BITCOINS 3,000,000', whereas v4.0 Block 630,000 reads '1.19 VMB' and '7.16 BTC BLOCK REWARD' (6.25 subsidy + 0.91 fees).
Do NOT use C2PA-modified copies in source/ for byte-level forensics; always use FractalEncrypt_FullNode_v4_original.png (27f4f01f...) and bitcoin-wheel-detail_original.svg (778b5caa...).
